narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 39% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help you succeed.

The most important factor influencing this prediction is your current lack of intention to pursue higher education after graduation. Among students who are not required to take remedial courses, every single one expressed a desire to continue their studies beyond high school. This difference strongly contributed to the model’s assessment that you may be at greater risk of not passing.

Another factor that played a significant role, but in a positive way, is your reason for choosing your current school. You selected your school based on its reputation, which is less common among students in your situation. This choice actually helped lower your risk, as students who value their school’s reputation tend to be more motivated and successful.

Additionally, your record of not having failed any classes in the past also worked in your favor. The average student in your position has not failed classes either, and this consistency helped reduce your predicted risk.

Given these factors, the requirement to take remedial courses is not a judgment of your abilities, but rather a precaution to ensure you have every opportunity to succeed. Taking advantage of these courses can help you strengthen your skills and reconsider your future educational goals, which may further improve your chances of passing and open up more opportunities after graduation.
